path.note: The end user's question, which can carry instructions or a url, goes into the chain
The model composes the request url using the question and the API docs

controls.name: configured_api_base
controls.note: The API base from config only shapes the docs in the prompt. Nothing enforces it on the fetched url, so it does not reduce this finding.

recommendations.complete_remediation: Give APIChain a required limit_to_domains allowlist and check the scheme and host of the model-written url against it before both get and aget, as upstream did. The app passes the configured weather API base. Defence in depth: block link-local and private addresses at the HTTP layer and do not follow redirects off the allowed host.

findings.rationale: APIChain fetches whatever url the model writes, so a question that carries an instruction or a url makes the server request internal hosts such as the instance metadata service. The assistant is meant to call one documented forecast API, but the chain can reach any host the operator's network can reach. That is a model-controlled action beyond the declared task with no deterministic gate, which is LLM03 excessive functionality. PERMISSIONS is also accepted because the fix is a reach restriction.

evidence.upstream_fix_summary: Added a mandatory limit_to_domains allowlist to APIChain and a scheme plus domain check before both the sync and async request.

sink: the answer that quotes the internal response is returned to the end user

path.note: The body fetched from the internal host (instance credentials) becomes api_response
The raw response is placed in the answer prompt with no filtering
The prompt holding the credentials is sent to the external model provider
The summary that repeats the credentials is returned to the end user

recommendations.complete_remediation: Stop the fetch at the source with the limit_to_domains check, which also stops the disclosure. If other hosts are ever allowed, drop responses that do not come from the documented API before they reach the answer prompt and filter credentials out of anything returned to the user.

findings.rationale: The response fetched from the internal host is handed to the answer chain unchanged, sent to the external model provider and summarized back to the end user. Instance credentials are operator secrets, and the end user and the model provider are not authorized recipients for them by the manifest. Nothing between the fetch and the reply filters or blocks the data, so this is LLM02 at the high level, linked to F1 which makes the fetch possible.
